contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #071: Koebe’s circle-domain conjecture.

The literal quotient-sphere, coordinate, tagged-path, per-visit toll, and gate framework of Koebe build/sections/01-topology.tex and 03-barriers.tex; no main uniformization or rigidity theorem is assumed.

definitions.G: the physical domain, identified with its open image in a compact metric topological sphere X
definitions.B: X minus G, compact totally disconnected dust
definitions.cost: domain arclength integral plus m at EVERY dust parameter time, with explicitly specified endpoint omissions
definitions.allowed: exact residual atomless and rational-interval incidence constraints after each finite deletion, with permitted finite-level-union tags
definitions.barrier: bounded smooth finite-energy coordinate, zero on E_star, one on a prescribed deeper collar, preserving P after countable flag enlargement

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 071 (Koebe’s circle-domain conjecture.; papers: Removable Boundaries and Rigidity of Circle Domains; Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/071.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
Every nonempty connected open subset of the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a circle domain. Source: Koebe 00-introduction.tex, main theorem. Not established by this audit.

If Omega and Omega_prime are circle domains and the boundary of Omega is conformally removable, every conformal equivalence from Omega onto Omega_prime is a Mobius transformation. Source: rigidity introduction.tex, main theorem. Not established by this audit.

Allowed tagged paths are stable under reversal, affine reparametrization, restriction, and countable concatenation of restrictions with finite domain length and only countably many extra parameter times, exactly as lem:path-stability.

For g >= c0 > 0 and m >= 0 in counting ell2, any sequence of allowed paths with domain endpoints and costs converging to finite A can be collar-spliced between distinct limiting dust endpoints, with both endpoint tolls omitted, at cost <= A+eta; the one-ended version holds from F when the dust endpoint is outside closure_X(F), preserving original dust avoidance and hit restrictions when joining collars avoid the hit curves. This is lem:collar-splicing.

Under lem:jump-removal, finitely many fixed positive-toll jump levels with E-to-C cost >= beta retain cost >= beta-Delta after ANY sufficiently fine new dust-disk jump cover with toll max(rho, sup{m(s): dist_X(s,V)<tau}), for every fixed rho,tau>0 and 0<Delta<beta.

For generic finite prior level tuples, physical domain length is finite, there are only finitely many pairwise disjoint subcontinua above each positive diameter, every subcontinuum is locally connected, nondegenerate components are countable, and weighted domain-plus-dust length obeys eq:weighted-level-bound. This is lem:level-continua.

The manuscript allowed tagged codes, occupation, per-visit costs, and specified endpoint and collar-hit restrictions are Borel as asserted in lem:path-coding. This remains a separate obligation for downstream path-law extraction; the new barrier proof will not use it.

Under the exact hypotheses of thm:barrier, for every eps>0 a compatible barrier and permitted penalty region satisfy controlled size <= 8 (norm(g)+norm(m)) + eps; 0<=u<=1, a_u=4m, and only support(m) is added to the flags.

Under the same full path-system and endpoint hypotheses as thm:barrier, for every kappa>1 and eta>0 there is a compatible barrier with 0<=u<=1, a_u=kappa m, added flags only support(m), and controlled size <= kappa (norm(g)+norm(m)) + eta. Consequently for every eps>0 the controlled size is <= norm(g)+norm(m)+eps, with a_u=(1+o(1))m. Universal proof, not a finite experiment.

For a bounded function v on a planar open set, if |v(x)-v(y)| <= integral_[x,y] h for every contained line segment and h is nonnegative Borel locally L2, then v is completed-Lebesgue measurable, belongs to W12_loc, and its Euclidean weak gradient norm is <=h almost everywhere. No measurability of a path-cost infimum is required.

For arbitrary nonnegative extended tolls, disjoint left internal visit indices, one junction index, and disjoint right internal visit indices have total toll equal to the sum of both internal tolls plus exactly one junction toll, with repeated image points not identified. Also, for kappa>1 and delta=(kappa-1)/(4kappa), kappa(1-2delta)-1=(kappa-1)/2>0.
No universal constant strictly smaller than 1 can replace the norm(g)+norm(m) coefficient in C_SHARP_BARRIER, even for an empty prior list, no gates, m=0, and a domain with a single dust component.

The positive-law alternative thm:positive-law extracts an L2 domain-occupation, counting-ell2 dust-hit law with the stated visit bounds and absolutely continuous tuple laws from failure of sufficiently small compatible barriers. Its full statement is an open downstream manuscript obligation.

The diffuse-intersection and four-path crossing construction proves thm:countable-exceptions, the countability of endpoints failing arbitrarily small compatible barriers. This downstream manuscript claim remains open in this audit.

The manuscript compact-arcs and period-one stream construction lem:compact-arcs and lem:stream produces the period-one compatible coordinates with the stated boundary measures and smoothing. This downstream manuscript claim remains open in this audit.

The later component-selection and retained-test uniformization construction collapses the selected complementary components while preserving the conformal and marked-test conclusions claimed by the Koebe manuscript. This is a downstream obligation, not established here.

The Koebe companion retained-test theorem and scalar retained-test corollary (generated references thm:retained-tests and cor:scalar-retained-tests, numbered 7.5 and 7.6) supply the scalar models used by rigidity prop:models. These conclusions remain unverified.

The rigidity companion prop:models obtains its required retained scalar models from the Koebe companion scalar retained-test construction; the model construction and its hypotheses remain an open dependency.

In Rajala arXiv:2408.12027v1 Section 4, transboundary admissibility sums a boundary weight once per visited complementary component, not once per parameter visit; Proposition 4.2 gives rectangular duality only under countable connectivity. These results do not by themselves prove the manuscript tagged per-visit compatible-barrier theorem.

claims.natural_statement: For arbitrary nonnegative extended tolls, disjoint left internal visit indices, one junction index, and disjoint right internal visit indices have total toll equal to the sum of both internal tolls plus exactly one junction toll, with repeated image points not identified. Also, for kappa>1 and delta=(kappa-1)/(4kappa), kappa(1-2delta)-1=(kappa-1)/2>0.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable section

namespace TaggedJumpAudit

theorem per_visit_glue {A I J : Type*} (w : A → ℝ≥0∞)
    (left : I → A) (p : A) (right : J → A) :
    (∑' t : I ⊕ (Unit ⊕ J),
      w (Sum.elim left (Sum.elim (fun _ : Unit => p) right) t)) =
      (∑' i, w (left i)) + w p + (∑' j, w (right j)) := by
  simp [tsum_sum, add_assoc]

theorem junction_paid {A I J : Type*} (w : A → ℝ≥0∞)
    (left : I → A) (p : A) (right : J → A)
    (budget : ℝ≥0∞) (hp : w p ≤ budget) :
    (∑' t : I ⊕ (Unit ⊕ J),
      w (Sum.elim left (Sum.elim (fun _ : Unit => p) right) t)) ≤
      (∑' i, w (left i)) + budget + (∑' j, w (right j)) := by
  rw [per_visit_glue]
  exact add_le_add_right (add_le_add_left hp _) _

theorem normalization_identity (k : ℝ) (hk : 1 < k) :
    k * (1 - 2 * ((k - 1) / (4 * k))) - 1 = (k - 1) / 2 := by
  have hk0 : k ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (lt_trans zero_lt_one hk)
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem normalization_positive (k : ℝ) (hk : 1 < k) :
    0 < k * (1 - 2 * ((k - 1) / (4 * k))) - 1 := by
  rw [normalization_identity k hk]
  linarith

theorem sharpness_deficit (n : ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    1 - (n / (n + 1)) ^ 2 = (2 * n + 1) / (n + 1) ^ 2 := by
  have hn1 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (by linarith)
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem sharpness_error_bound (n : ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    1 - (n / (n + 1)) ^ 2 < 2 / (n + 1) := by
  rw [sharpness_deficit n hn]
  have hn1 : 0 < n + 1 := by linarith
  apply (div_lt_iff₀ (sq_pos_of_pos hn1)).2
  field_simp
  nlinarith

end TaggedJumpAudit

external_assumptions.statement: Connected relatively open subsets of a locally connected compact metric continuum are arcwise connected, and a path in a Hausdorff space contains a simple arc between distinct endpoints.
